note: A fixture that names a real component takes its element shape FROM THAT COMPONENT — rendered, then pasted — never from the CSS. Deriving the shape from the CSS is what let `button-modern-md` and `input-modern-md` sit on `.ds-btn`/`.ds-input` for months: a selector states what an element must carry to be MATCHED, and says nothing about whether any component emits it, so a CSS-derived fixture can measure a rule that never paints and still look green. Regenerate a component shape by rendering the engine implementation with `renderToStaticMarkup` and pasting the result, minus React-generated ids, plus `data-probe`. The synthetic fixtures (the two skeleton controls and the token readout) are exempt: they exist to read a dial, not to stand for a component. `requiresSelectors` is not documentation either: the harness asserts each string occurs verbatim in the CSS it is about to measure and marks the fixture `unmatched` if it does not, so a fixture that stops being matched is reported, never silently measured as zero. Pin selectors and the paint statement, never a declaration's VALUE — a precedence ruling would then read as a broken fixture.

fixtures.why: The modern Button as the engine actually renders it. Until 2026-08-11 this fixture carried `.ds-btn`, a RUSTIC theme rule no component can produce (both engines render `rottay-button--{modern,rustic}`), so every reading attributed to 'the modern button' measured a rule that never paints. The token defect it exposed happened to be real, which is the dangerous case: a lying instrument that returns a true finding teaches you to trust it. Chain: border-radius <- --_ds-button-resolved-radius <- the size rule's precedence between --ds-button-md-radius and --ds-radius-md.

targets.why: The button root IS its own hit target -- no separate expanded touch-area wrapper exists in the modern engine's markup, so this target reads the same element as `root` under a name that says what it is being asked for: real sizing geometry rather than paint. `@rect-inline-size`/`@rect-block-size` are read from getBoundingClientRect, so a padding/border/transform mutation that changes what actually renders cannot hide behind an unmoved computed longhand.

fixtures.why: The modern Input as the engine actually renders it, inside the field wrapper it always ships with — the root IS the input element, not a container. Carried `.ds-input` until 2026-08-11 for the same reason the button did, and was wrong the same way. A distinct chrome family for the colour channels, and a third radius chain: border-radius <- --ds-input-resolved-radius <- the size rule's precedence between --ds-input-md-radius and --ds-radius-md.

THE POSITIVE CONTROL. This rule reads the dial DIRECTLY -- `calc(4px * var(--ds-radius-scale, 1))` -- with no derived token in between. If this element does not move when the dial turns, the harness itself is broken and every 'inert' verdict in the same run is void.
Second direct dial consumer on a different literal -- `calc(6px * var(--ds-radius-scale, 1))`. Two controls, two literals: a single moving fixture cannot be a coincidence of one rule.

Not a component: a bare element inside the tenant scope whose custom properties are read directly. It answers 'what value does this token RESOLVE to for this tenant' without an intervening paint rule, which separates 'the token is wrong' from 'the component does not read it'. Extended 2026-08-11 with the rhythm pair -- --ds-rhythm-scale is the raw tenant input (enum stop or override), --ds-rhythm-effective-scale is the clamped 0.8..1.25 channel every consume site reads -- so a causal rhythm run has a direct-read control fixture on the SAME element as the radius readout, rather than needing a second synthetic fixture for a second control.

The modern Flex as the engine actually renders it, with a preset ('md') uniform gap. Chain: gap <- calc(--ds-flex-gap * --ds-rhythm-effective-scale). One hop: the scaled rule multiplies the md rung directly by the tenant rhythm dial in the gap declaration itself, held at the base rule's specificity by `:where()` so source order -- not escalation -- decides. Proves the rhythm dial reaches Flex's layout gap the way the six fixtures above prove the radius dial reaches radius.

The modern Grid as the engine actually renders it, with a preset ('md') gap routed through --ds-grid-gap rather than the inline gap a numeric measurement would use. Chain: gap <- calc(--ds-grid-gap * --ds-rhythm-effective-scale). One hop, anchored on the engine class (rottay-grid--modern) rather than a repeated attribute, so the scaled rule outranks the unscaled base rule by source order alone -- the same law Flex's `:where()` enforces by specificity parity instead.

The modern Stack as the engine actually renders it, with a preset ('md') spacing rung -- the one layout primitive where rhythm reaches the paint with no inline value at all: the data-spacing attribute alone selects the scaled rule. Chain: gap <- var(--_ds-stack-gap-current) <- calc(--ds-spacing-4 * --ds-rhythm-effective-scale). Two hops, one more than Flex/Grid/Space, because the rung is mirrored into a private channel so the divider can center itself inside the same governed rhythm instead of adding its own separation on top of it.

The modern Space as the engine actually renders it, with a preset ('md') gap. Chain: gap <- calc(--ds-space-instance-gap * --ds-density-effective-scale * --ds-rhythm-effective-scale). One hop, but the only one of the four where rhythm compounds with density in the same declaration -- density sizes the md token, rhythm sizes the room around it -- held at the base rule's specificity by `:where()` so source order decides, exactly as Flex's split-gap rules do.
requiresSelectors: gap: calc(var(--ds-space-instance-gap, var(--ds-space-small-size, var(--ds-spacing-2))) * var(--ds-density-effective-scale) * var(--ds-rhythm-effective-scale, 1))

fixtures.why: The negative half of flex-modern-preset-gap: the modern Flex with a NUMERIC gap (8), not a preset rung. `resolveFlexAttributes`/`flexGapPresetSpelling` stamp NO data-gap-preset for a number (the function returns undefined for typeof 'number'), so the rhythm-scaled rule cannot match at all -- only the unscaled base rule `.rottay-flex[data-gap='uniform'] { gap: var(--ds-flex-gap); }` reaches it. Proves numeric-instance-gaps-exact instead of asserting it in prose.

The negative half of grid-modern-preset-gap: the modern Grid with a NUMERIC gap (8), not a preset rung. A numeric grid gap never reaches --ds-grid-gap or a data-gap-preset attribute at all -- `buildGridStyles` writes it as a plain inline `gap` CSS property, the strongest position in the cascade, so no stylesheet rule (scaled or not) can reach it. Proves numeric-instance-gaps-exact instead of asserting it in prose.

The negative half of stack-modern-preset-gap: the modern Stack with a NUMERIC gap (8), which stamps `data-spacing='custom'` rather than a named rung. `.rottay-stack[data-spacing='custom']` has specificity (0,2,0) and carries no `:where(.rottay-stack--modern)` scaled companion, so it outranks the unscoped modern-default override at (0,1,0) and reads the caller's own --ds-stack-gap channel with no rhythm multiplication anywhere in the chain. Proves numeric-instance-gaps-exact instead of asserting it in prose.

The negative half of space-modern-preset-gap: the modern Space with a NUMERIC size (8), not a preset spelling. The bare number lands in `data-size` unmatched by the enumerated `:where([data-size='small'], ..., [data-size='lg'])` scaled-rule list, so only the unscaled root rule `gap: var(--ds-space-instance-gap, ...)` reaches it. Proves numeric-instance-gaps-exact instead of asserting it in prose.
